Kinsley / procurement team,

Appreciate the specifics — below is an operational answer on GPU fitment, packing assumptions, and a reservation plan you can evaluate. I've attached a short pricing scenarios CSV and our slotting playbook for reference.

Executive summary (quick):
- Recommended steady pool: 6x H100 (80GB) nodes running quantized FP16->int8 pipelines where safe. This yields reliable headroom for 2,500 rpm under your latency SLOs with conservative packing.
- Burst plan: reserve an additional 3x A100s (40GB) or use Redwood burst-on-demand lanes that map to on-demand H100s in our hosted pool for short campaigns.
- Lower-cost option (if budget constrained): 10x RTX6000-equivalent V: higher packing variance and risk at tail latencies; recommend only for non-customer-facing batch/reranking workloads.

Throughput guidance (approximate, per-GPU delivered inference capacity for Llama-3-70B quantized):
- H100 (80GB, int8 optimized): ~18-22 requests/sec (@ avg prompt+completion ~800 tokens)
- A100 (40GB, FP16): ~10-12 requests/sec (with larger batch gains if you accept higher P50)
- RTX-class (32GB, mixed-precision): ~6-8 requests/sec; good for embeddings/reranking, not primary chat SLOs

Packing and quantization assumptions:
- We assume int8 quantization for the primary model where internal evals show <2% quality delta for your prompt set. That drives ~1.7x packing improvement vs FP16 in our benchmarks.
- For tail-latency-sensitive routes, we recommend reserving a small dedicated slot-per-request headroom (we show this as 10% extra capacity in the workbook).

Reservation recommendation (12-month):
- Commit: 6x H100 steady + 3x A100 hot-standby (reserve pricing tier 2).
- Burst: Redwood-managed burst lane to on-demand H100s (billed at on-demand rate) for short windows up to 4x baseline.
- Fallbacks: If an H100 node is saturated, requests flow to A100 hot-standby; if A100s are saturated, Redwood routes requests to compatible quantized 2nd-tier models (smaller families) to preserve availability (graceful degradation).

Pricing tradeoffs (high-level):
- Reserved-only (all H100): best unit cost but higher upfront commitment.
- Hybrid reserved (H100 steady + A100 standby + managed burst): reduces commit while preserving average cost 12-20% above full-reserve, with strong tail protection.
- On-demand-centric: highest unit cost but zero commit and fastest scale for unpredictable bursts.

Next steps we propose:
1) Workshop on Thursday 15:00 PT to walk the workbook and calibrate pack factors against your test prompts.
2) After the workshop, we’ll produce a draft SOW + reservation cost matrix (we can use SOW_draft_template.docx as the starting point).

Attachments referenced: reservation_pricing_scenarios.csv, slotting_playbook.md.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated & Pricing | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
